basis: taxonomy.json VOC-BAND-v1.1 SUP definitions and resolution_rules
rule: Written and frozen before any encoder run. Encoder prompts contain only CODING-CONTRACT.md and taxonomy.json, never this file.

cases.text: I've been living in this band since 30 weeks and the weight off my lower back is unreal. I can stand at the stove again without needing to sit down every five minutes.

expected_sup.span: the weight off my lower back

optional_other.note: can stand at the stove again

cases.reason: Step 2 weight/load transfer ('weight off') outranks step 3 explicit back reference ('lower back'). This is the B05 pattern. A BACK code on the same span is the old-definition error.

cases.scenario: back plus lifted belly in one record
cases.text: It lifts my bump nicely, and my lower back pain has eased by the end of the day.

expected_sup.span: my lower back pain has eased

cases.reason: Two coordinated predicates, two attributes, two distinct spans. Step 1 takes the belly clause. The back clause has explicit back + pain relief and no weight/load term, so step 3 BACK applies; step 4 PRESSURE is blocked by its 'no back reference' guard.

cases.text: It really takes the pressure off my hips, especially by the end of the day.

expected_sup.span: takes the pressure off my hips

cases.reason: Step 2 'pressure off'. No back reference and no belly lift, so BACK/GENERAL cannot apply.

cases.scenario: supports my back, no weight-transfer semantics
cases.text: It gives my back solid support and keeps me sitting up straight at my desk.
cases.reason: Explicit 'my back' + support, no weight/load transfer, so step 3 BACK. The generic word 'support' must not also produce GENERAL: the priority order makes BACK the only SUP code for this span.

cases.scenario: belly held up, no explicit support force
cases.text: It holds my belly up so it isn't hanging so low anymore, and that alone is a relief.
cases.reason: Step 1 'holds my belly up'. The trailing 'relief' has no pain or pressure object and no back reference, so step 4 must not fire; GENERAL is excluded by step 1. Risk: over-broad reading of 'relief' as PRESSURE_OFFLOAD.

cases.text: It's really supportive and I feel much more secure with it on.
cases.reason: Only a generic support evaluation. No body part, no weight/load, no belly lift, so step 5 GENERAL. 'secure' is not STB: STB needs a slip/roll/move cue.

cases.text: Almost fully takes away the sciatica I've had since my second trimester.

expected_sup.span: Almost fully takes away the sciatica

cases.reason: Step 4 'take away' + pain (sciatica), no back reference, so PRESSURE_OFFLOAD. 'Almost fully' is a quotable degree reservation on the same attribute, so the contract requires qualified_positive, not positive.

cases.text: It supports my back well, but it rolls down every time I sit.

expected_sup.span: rolls down every time I sit

cases.reason: Positive and negative are on different attributes; the contract says split into two aspects with their own spans. BACK stays positive, not mixed or qualified_positive. Risk: the encoder may collapse the contrast into one mixed BACK aspect.
